src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:480-486 float_literal_text returns f"{value:.16e}". Python's 'e' spec with precision 16 gives 1 + 16 = 17 significant digits in exponent form with at least a two-digit signed exponent. 0.5 -> 5.0000000000000000e-01. 1e-05 is the double 1.00000000000000008180...e-05, so it rounds to 1.0000000000000001e-05 and -1e-05 gives -1.0000000000000001e-05. 17 significant digits round-trip a double. MySQL treats a literal with an exponent as a double (approximate value). _number (472-477) splits a leading minus into Neg over the positive literal. Tests at tests/unit/test_row_rules.py:325-339 assert the same format. I did not run the code or MySQL, and I did not check criterion 13's wording.

rule_sets.py:1046-1052 selects DATA_TYPE from information_schema.COLUMNS, passes it through _text (line 988-989, decodes bytes) and .lower(); line 1088 compares it with VALUE_TYPE_DATA_TYPES (lines 177-182), whose members are lowercase names (tinyint, smallint, mediumint, int, bigint, float, double, char, varchar, tinytext, text, mediumtext, longtext, enum). MySQL 8 information_schema.COLUMNS.DATA_TYPE holds the bare lowercase type name (e.g. 'int', 'enum', 'varchar', 'tinyint' for tinyint(1)), so the names match; lowercasing makes the match robust either way.

_Compiler._node (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:567-636) builds rules only from EQ/NEQ/LT/LTE/GT/GTE (_COMPARISONS, :454), IN, AND, OR and EXISTS. It never emits NOT, IS NULL, COALESCE or a null-safe comparison, so the formula is monotone in three-valued logic: a comparison on NULL yields NULL (unknown), which stays non-true through AND/OR (OR with another true branch is true for that other branch, not for the NULL comparison). Traced `!=` on a NULL status inside any_of/all_of: NEQ(NULL,'x') is NULL, so it contributes nothing. owner_via with NULL id_column (:585-596): EQ(link.row_col, s.id_col) is NULL, so the EXISTS subquery finds no row. inherit and referenced_by also use EQ joins (:597-635). The condition is applied as a WHERE clause (safety/rule_sets.py:420), which keeps only true rows. The only IS NULL/NULL use in safety/rule_sets.py:549,568 concerns unlisted-column projection, not the row rule. Absolute-claim trace: the NULL != case inside any_of/all_of and the NULL id_column owner_via case both fail to make the row visible. The claim holds.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:405-422 _scoped_body builds SELECT <listed columns> FROM name AS sl<k>_0 WHERE <rule> LIMIT 18446744073709551615. _rewrite (583-599) replaces every base table reference that has a rule with this body via _wrap (453-468), which keeps the model's alias and moves joins of a parenthesized join out of the derived table, so the model's ON clause or correlated subquery can only reference the derived table's output columns, which are rows that already passed the rule. The model's expressions never see the raw table. The LIMIT blocks derived-table merging and condition pushdown, so the rule filter is applied before any model expression. Absolute-claim input traced: a model expression such as 1/0 in a scoped table's ON clause, and a correlated subquery referencing the scoped alias. Both read the derived alias, so neither reaches a hidden row. The same shape (LIMIT) is used for catalog views (575-580). Caveat: the MySQL optimizer behaviour (no merge or pushdown with LIMIT) was not run here. It is read from the code's design and docstring, not tested against a server.
